items.phrase: God, in predestinating, or condemning, had in no wise regard to the works
items.why: Reported as what 'the most wicked heretics' say; the decree calls it profane and impious.

items.phrase: the Divine Will is thus solely and without cause the author of their condemnation
items.why: A rejected claim posed inside a rhetorical question ('what greater calumny').

items.phrase: to have fallen from his perfection and impassibility
items.why: Impassibility is predicated of unfallen man, not of God.

items.phrase: hallowed by the invocation of the Holy Spirit
items.why: The sacrament is hallowed; holiness is not predicated of God here.

items.phrase: are severed and divided by the hands and teeth, though in accident only
items.why: About the eucharistic Body under the accidents of bread; not divine simplicity.

items.phrase: there is not a part of the Body and Blood of the Lord
items.why: 'Not a part' concerns the sacramental Body, not God being without parts.

items.phrase: it is one and the same Christ that is truly and really present
items.why: 'Truly present' is about eucharistic presence, not God's truth or faithfulness.

items.phrase: are, of necessity, subject to eternal punishment
items.why: Eternal is predicated of punishment of the unregenerate, not of God.

items.phrase: it is impossible for her to in any wise err
items.why: Infallibility is predicated of the Church ('her').

items.phrase: or to at all deceive, or be deceived
items.why: Truthfulness predicated of the Church, not of God.

items.phrase: is a living image of God upon the earth
items.why: The Bishop is called a living image of God; the family concerns the Son as image of the Father.

items.phrase: the fountain of the Divine Mysteries and graces
items.why: The High Priest is the fountain of the Mysteries; not God as fountain of being.

items.phrase: there remaineth in them neither understanding nor light, but only darkness and blindness
items.why: Light is denied of heretics; nothing is predicated of the Son as Light.

items.phrase: they could not be judged by the Church
items.why: The Church judges; the family is God as Judge.

items.phrase: the faith which is in us, justifieth through works, with Christ
items.why: 'Justifieth' is soteriological (faith justifies), not the justice of God.

items.phrase: by [observing] the Divine commandments, justifieth us with Christ
items.why: Faith working by love justifies; not a predicate of God.

items.phrase: under which they are visible and tangible
items.why: The accidents of bread and wine are visible; not a statement about God's invisibility.

items.phrase: of the most holy Theotokos, and of all the saints, also of the holy Angels
items.why: Holy is predicated of the Theotokos, saints and angels.

items.phrase: conferred in the name of the Holy Trinity
items.why: 'Holy' appears only inside the title 'Holy Trinity'; nothing is asserted about holiness.

items.phrase: then remission of sin throuhgh the Spirit is true also
items.why: 'True' = real/valid, predicated of remission of sin (source spelling preserved).

items.phrase: by the imposition of hands and the invocation of the All-holy Spirit
items.why: 'All-holy' is a fixed title of the Spirit inside a description of ordination; not an assertion of the predicate.

items.phrase: it delivereth him from the eternal punishment, to which he was liable
items.why: Baptism delivers from eternal punishment; eternity is not predicated of God.

items.phrase: the invisible are the angelic powers, rational souls, and demons
items.why: Invisibility is predicated of angels, souls and demons, not of God.

items.locator: Formula of Concord, Epitome: XII. Other Sects, ¶25–31
items.phrase: That Christ is not true, essential, natural God
items.why: A New Arian error listed in order to be condemned.

items.locator: Formula of Concord, Epitome: XII. Other Sects, ¶25–31
items.phrase: there is not one only, eternal, divine essence of the Father Son, and Holy Ghost
items.why: Anti-Trinitarian error listed for condemnation; eternal essence is denied by the opponent, not asserted.

items.locator: Formula of Concord, Epitome: XII. Other Sects, ¶25–31
items.phrase: all three of equal power, wisdom, majesty, and glory
items.why: Part of the reported Anti-Trinitarian view (three separate essences of equal power); not the standard's assertion.

items.locator: Formula of Concord, Solid Declaration: XII. Other Sects, ¶31–39
items.phrase: That the Father alone is true God.
items.why: Listed Anti-Trinitarian error; the standard rejects it.

items.locator: Formula of Concord, Solid Declaration: XII. Other Sects, ¶8–15
items.phrase: are holy and the children of God even without and before Baptism
items.why: Anabaptist error about children; holiness predicated of children in a rejected view.

items.locator: Formula of Concord, Solid Declaration: XII. Other Sects, ¶16–30
items.phrase: regard Christ according to the flesh, or His assumed humanity, as a creature
items.why: Schwenckfeldian error reported; 'creature' concerns Christ's flesh in a condemned view.

items.locator: Formula of Concord, Epitome: XII. Other Sects, ¶1–10
items.phrase: That Christ is not true God
items.why: Anabaptist error listed for condemnation.

items.locator: Augsburg Confession: Article I. Of God, ¶1–6
items.phrase: the Manichaeans, who assumed two principles, one Good and the other Evil
items.why: Manichaean view condemned; 'Good' is a rejected principle, not a predicate of God asserted here.

items.locator: Augsburg Confession: Article I. Of God, ¶1–6
items.phrase: “Word” signifies a spoken word
items.why: Samosatene view condemned; the standard denies this reading of 'Word'.

items.locator: Augsburg Confession: Article III. Of the Son of God, ¶1–6
items.phrase: did assume the human nature in the womb of the blessed Virgin Mary
items.why: The incarnation of the Son in a body says nothing about God being without body.

items.locator: Apology of the Augsburg Confession: Article II (I). Of Original Sin, ¶4–7
items.phrase: no one is condemned to eternal death on account of original sin
items.why: The adversaries' claim, reported to be refuted; eternal death is not a predicate of God.

items.locator: Augsburg Confession: Article II. Of Original Sin, ¶1–3
items.phrase: bringing eternal death upon those not born again through Baptism
items.why: Eternal is predicated of death/punishment, not of God.

items.locator: Apology of the Augsburg Confession: Article IV-b. Of Love and the Fulfilling of the Law, ¶58–60
items.phrase: the Law condemns all men
items.why: The Law condemns; God as Judge is not the subject.

items.phrase: we profess to be one, holy, catholic and apostolic
items.why: Holy is a mark of the Church.

items.phrase: is held, as a matter of faith, to be unfailingly holy
items.why: The Church is unfailingly holy; not a predicate of God.

items.phrase: Jesus Christ is true God and true man
items.why: 'True God' = genuinely God (Christological), not God's truthfulness/authenticity as the family defines it.

items.phrase: composed of rational soul and body
items.why: Chalcedon on Christ's humanity; nothing about God being incorporeal.

items.phrase: is endowed with a true human knowledge
items.why: Christ's human soul's knowledge; not divine wisdom.

items.phrase: United with Christ, the Church is sanctified by him
items.why: Holiness of the Church.

items.locator: Article XXVIII (28) — Of The Lord'S Supper
items.phrase: only after an heavenly and spiritual manner
items.why: 'Spiritual manner' of receiving the Body of Christ; not God named as spirit.

items.locator: Article II (2) — Of The Word Or Son Of God, Which Was Made Very Man
items.phrase: who truly suffered, was crucified, dead, and buried
items.why: Christ's suffering in his manhood; not a statement that God is without passions.

items.locator: Outline of the Faith (BCP p. 854) — The Church: Q. Why is the Church described as holy?
items.phrase: The Church is holy, because the Holy Spirit dwells in it
items.why: Holiness predicated of the Church.

items.locator: Outline of the Faith (BCP p. 845) — Human Nature: Q. What are we by nature?
items.phrase: We are part of God’s creation, made in the image of God
items.why: Humanity in God's image; the family concerns the Son as image of the Father.

items.locator: Catechism, Q.5 — "Rehearse the Articles of thy Belief."
items.phrase: The holy Catholick Church
items.why: Creed clause about the Church.

items.phrase: a holy congregation and gathering of true Christian believers
items.why: Holy is predicated of the Church.

items.locator: Article 19: The Two Natures of Christ
items.phrase: retains all that belongs to a real body
items.why: Christ's human nature has a real body; nothing about God without body.

items.locator: Article 29: The Marks of the True Church
items.phrase: what is the true church
items.why: 'True church' — genuineness of the Church, not God's truth.

items.phrase: preserves for himself a community chosen for eternal life and united in true faith
items.why: Eternal life of the elect; eternity is not predicated of God.

items.phrase: endued with knowledge, righteousness, and true holiness, after his own image
items.why: Holiness of created humanity.

items.phrase: which was subject unto change
items.why: Man's will subject to change; the opposite pole of immutability, predicated of man.

items.phrase: The catholic or universal church, which is invisible
items.why: Invisibility predicated of the invisible church.

items.phrase: with all the essential properties, and common infirmities thereof
items.why: Christ's assumed human nature with its infirmities; not divine impassibility.

items.phrase: this holy church is not confined, bound, or limited to a certain place
items.why: Non-circumscription predicated of the Church, not of God.

items.phrase: all Scripture is totally true and trustworthy
items.why: Truth predicated of Scripture.

items.phrase: truth, without any mixture of error, for its matter
items.why: Truthfulness predicated of the Bible.

items.phrase: Man is the special creation of God, made in His own image
items.why: Image predicated of man.

items.phrase: bring man into His holy fellowship
items.why: 'Holy fellowship' is a descriptor of fellowship; holiness is not asserted of God as a proposition.

items.phrase: the Bible is the divinely inspired word of God
items.why: 'Word of God' names Scripture, not the Son as Logos.

items.locator: Article II — Of the Word, or Son of God, Who Was Made Very Man
items.phrase: who truly suffered, was crucified, dead, and buried
items.why: Christ suffered in his manhood; not divine impassibility.

items.locator: Article III — Of the Resurrection of Christ
items.phrase: took again his body, with all things appertaining to the perfection of man's nature
items.why: Christ's risen body; nothing about God being without body.

items.phrase: We believe it is one, holy, apostolic and catholic
items.why: Marks of the Church.

items.locator: Article XII — The Judgment and the Future State
items.phrase: the righteous to life eternal and the wicked to endless condemnation
items.why: Eternal life/condemnation of people.

items.locator: Article 6. Creation and Calling of Human Beings
items.phrase: We believe that God has created human beings in the divine image
items.why: Image predicated of human beings; the family concerns the Son.

items.locator: Article 6. Creation and Calling of Human Beings
items.phrase: human beings were created good, in the image of God
items.why: Goodness predicated of created humanity.

items.phrase: The church, the body of Christ, is called to become ever more like Jesus Christ
items.why: Likeness to Christ predicated of the church.

items.phrase: hinder not the Church from being holy
items.why: Holiness of the Church.

items.phrase: the Catholic Church can not sin, nor err, nor utter falsehood in place of truth
items.why: Infallibility/truthfulness of the Church.

items.phrase: is at the same time invisible, so far as she is also partially in heaven
items.why: Invisibility of the Church.

items.phrase: In one, holy, catholic and apostolic Church
items.why: Creed clause about the Church.

items.phrase: created in the image and likeness of God
items.why: Image predicated of man.

items.locator: Definition of Faith, Council of Chalcedon (451), paragraph 8
items.phrase: made in all things like unto us, sin only excepted
items.why: Christ's real humanity (Chalcedon, Percival); nothing about God being incorporeal. Re-cut from the OCA paraphrase when the row was re-sourced for v2.25.

authoring: Hand-authored from corpus text by the Gate 6 build session; each phrase re-asserted verbatim against its chunk at build.
